results.excerpt: Rate limit incident Q3 2024: API consumers were not warned 24 hours before the rate limit threshold was lowered from 1000 to 500 requests per minute. Several clients experienced outages lasting 2-4 hours.
Lessons learned: (1) All limit changes require 72-hour advance notice. (2) Clients must have a documented escalation path. (3) Rate limit headers should be included in all API responses.
API versioning policy: breaking changes require a deprecation notice period of at least 30 days. Rate limit adjustments are considered breaking changes when they reduce the existing limit.

output_document.summary: Multiple semantic retrieval passes and direct entry reads were performed against the 'glamup' project store searching for FashionMate's error-to-HTTP-status-code mapping rules. The corpus contains only three documents (a Q3 2024 rate-limit incident report, a postmortem lessons document, and API versioning guidelines) plus one repeated decision entry stating that all API inputs are validated against a JSON schema and empty arrays are rejected (updated 2024-11-01). No document recording how FashionMate translates specific error conditions (such as missing or empty content) into HTTP status codes was found. This is a documentation gap that must be addressed—either by retrieving the rule from the FashionMate team directly or by formally documenting an agreed-upon mapping—before the GlamUp no-content crash fix can be planned with confidence.
